findings.title: Removed 'creating'/'deleting' rule states handling causes loss of UX feedback
findings.body: The old code compared ruler rules against prom rules to detect rules that are being created (present in ruler but not yet in Prometheus) or deleted (present in Prometheus but removed from ruler) and rendered RuleOperationListItem/operation=Creating/Deleting accordingly. The new implementation only renders from the Prometheus response and no longer fetches/compares the ruler group, so rules in the process of being created or deleted will simply not appear or appear with no special indication, changing user-visible behavior during rule creation/deletion.

findings.title: Edit/view URL no longer includes returnTo parameter
findings.body: The removed GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx built the view href with `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`, preserving navigation context. The new GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx builds the href with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` without passing returnTo, so users navigating from the rule list to the detail view and back may lose their previous location/filter state.

findings.title: isPaused no longer falls back to rulerRule.is_paused
findings.body: Previously isPaused used `rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused` combining both prom and ruler sources. Now it's just `rule?.isPaused` from the GrafanaPromRuleDTO. Since the ruler lookup is removed entirely, this is likely fine, but if the Prometheus rule briefly lacks the isPaused field (e.g. stale response), the pause state indicator could be incorrect with no fallback.

findings.title: Deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities still exported without migration path enforced
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities is marked @deprecated but is still used elsewhere (e.g. RulesTable via useAlertRuleAbility) and now internally forwards to useAllRulerRuleAbilities with a derived groupIdentifier. This dual-path (rulerRule vs promRule abilities) risks diverging behavior between RuleActionsButtons (old table) and the new RuleActionsButtons.V2/AlertRuleMenu, since permissions can now be computed via two independent paths that must be kept consistent manually.
